children: , the data-center networking and custom-silicon designer, traded at $271.19 at 10.50am EST, down approximately 1.3% on Friday, October 9, as investors weighed ambitious growth plans against an already demanding valuation. According to Investor's Business Daily, the company's investor-day forecasts prompted analysts to raise their price targets. The valuation snapshot puts shares 119.94% above the $123.30 GF Value, suggesting a substantial growth premium is already baked in.

Management's investor-day presentation laid out a $20 billion revenue goal for fiscal 2028, with $18 billion coming from data centers. That compares with fiscal 2026 revenue of $8.2 billion overall and $6.1 billion from data centers. The total-sales target requires roughly 56% annual compounded growth over two years. Further out, management sees fiscal 2031 revenue reaching $70 billion to $90 billion. Those are company targets, and hitting them demands sustained execution as the business scales.

The analyst targets cited by Investor's Business Daily span $270 at Goldman Sachs, $350 at TD Cowen and $425 at Oppenheimer. At $271.19, shares already sit near Goldman's objective. The higher targets leave considerably more upside, but depend on stronger expectations for custom accelerators, optical connectivity and networking. That spread frames the investment debate: how much of the AI spending boom can Marvell turn into revenue and earnings? With a hefty valuation premium already in place, delivery matters more than another big forecast.

title: Marvell Stocks Fall as $20 Billion Goal Tests Execution
